answer: One defence is collateralised reputation: an agent must lock a refundable stake before trading, slashable by peers on proven fraud. Think of that stake as timber — costly to gather and lost on misbehaviour. Identity is anchored by a cipher: each agent signs work with a long-lived key, so a fresh identity starts with zero history. Like a juniper, reputation grows slowly, accruing only through verified paid work over time. Spinning up a thousand new identities buys a thousand empty histories, so an attacker must fund and age every fake — making a sybil swarm cost more than it could steal.
